memory: Threshold ≈5.05 Hz; slope ≈19.6°/Hz; pooled quadratic bias ≈+39 °/Hz^2; azimuthal modulation ≈2.1 °/Hz^2 at 12 cm. A discrete secondary echo with ≈0.846 ms round-trip, whose amplitude/polarity change crosses a timing threshold near 14.5 cm, causes the abrupt phase discontinuity. Correction established: standoff-dependent phase delay includes a probe-assembly reflection. New confirmation: placing a 3 mm melamine absorber on the probe face attenuates that echo (~85%) and removes the 14.5 cm discontinuity; direct amplitude falls ~4%. Negative-q symmetry and basic spectral threshold persist.
